title: A central extension of tori is a torus
statement: Let $k$ be an arbitrary field [def-weil-field]. All groups below are affine $k$-group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and subgroups are closed subgroup schemes [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Smoothness and connectedness mean [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme]. A torus is a group scheme whose extension to an algebraic closure $\bar k$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure] is isomorphic to $\mathbf G_m^r$ for some integer $r\geq0$ [def-sfb-tori-multiplicative-type, def-sc-gm-ga]. Let $E$ be smooth and connected, let $T\hookrightarrow E$ be a central torus subgroup, and let $q:E\to S$ be a faithfully flat finitely presented homomorphism to a torus $S$ with scheme-theoretic kernel exactly $T$. Here central means that $t e=e t$ in $E(A)$ for every commutative $k$-algebra $A$, $t\in T(A)$ and $e\in E(A)$; the kernel is the fibre of $q$ over the identity [def-pc-fibre-product]. Faithfully flat means flat and surjective [def-weil-flat-morphism], and finitely presented means locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Then $E$ is a torus over $k$.

source.place: Lemma 16.43, printed p.340, with ambient connected group G=E, H=E, H-prime=T; multiplicative-type conclusion together with smooth connectedness and Theorem 12.23, printed p.240, gives a torus. This is the inverse-image argument used in Theorem 17.82, printed p.379.

proof.text: Fix an algebraic closure $F=\bar k$. The identity $e:\operatorname{Spec}k\to E$ is a section of the structure morphism of the connected scheme $E$, so [lem-sbc-connected-rational-point-geometrically-connected] shows that $E\times_kK$ is connected for every field extension $K/k$. In particular $E_F$ is connected, and it is geometrically connected over $F$: an extension $L/F$ is also an extension of $k$, and $(E_F)_L\cong E_L$ by iterated base change [def-pc-fibre-product]. By clause (2) of [lem-pc-proper-base-change], it is smooth. All scalar-extended groups are affine of finite type: [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] identifies their rings with $F\otimes_k k[G]$, which are generated over $F$ by the images of any finite set of $k$-algebra generators of $k[G]$. Base change of the group-law diagrams gives their group structures [def-sc-group-scheme].

source.place: Lemma 16.43, p.340, via Corollaries 12.41 (with Chapter 12 erratum) and 12.22, pp.244,239; diagonalizable classification, pp.231--234,240.

proof.text: The map $q^*:k[S]\to k[E]$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-iff-flat-affine], and faithfully flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-surjective-spectrum-faithfully-flat], since $q$ is surjective. Its scalar extension $q_F^*:F[S_F]\to F[E_F]$ is faithfully flat by [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-base-change], using the tensor-ring identification of [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. In this identification it is base change along $k[S]\to F\otimes_k k[S]$. The kernel is $T_F$: both this kernel and the base change of $T=E\times_{S,e}\operatorname{Spec}k$ represent the pairs consisting of an $E_F$-point with image the identity, by the fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product]. Centrality persists, since an $F$-algebra is also a $k$-algebra and $T_F(A)=T(A)$, $E_F(A)=E(A)$.

source.place: Lemma 16.43, p.340, via Corollaries 12.41 (with Chapter 12 erratum) and 12.22, pp.244,239; diagonalizable classification, pp.231--234,240.

proof.text: By the torus hypothesis [def-sfb-tori-multiplicative-type], $T_F$ and $S_F$ are split tori. The formula $D_F(\mathbf Z^r)\simeq\mathbf G_m^r$ in [lem-sfb-diagonalizable-group-geometric-criteria] makes them groups of multiplicative type in the sense required by [lem-sfb-multiplicative-extension-action-rigidity]. Apply that lemma to $G=E_F$, $N=T_F$, $Q=S_F$ and the conjugation action of $E_F$ on itself. The action preserves $T_F$ because it is central, and consists of automorphisms by the group identities. Step 1 gives smoothness and connectedness of the acting group; step 2 supplies the faithfully flat quotient with precisely the indicated central kernel. The lemma gives $ghg^{-1}=h$ on every algebra of points. Multiplying by $g$ on the right gives $gh=hg$, hence $E_F$ is commutative [def-sc-group-scheme].

source.place: Lemma 16.43, p.340, via Corollaries 12.41 (with Chapter 12 erratum) and 12.22, pp.244,239; diagonalizable classification, pp.231--234,240.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-commutative-multiplicative-type-extension] to $q_F:E_F\to S_F$. Step 2 supplies its faithfully flat coordinate map and kernel $T_F$; step 3 supplies commutativity and the multiplicative-type hypotheses on kernel and quotient. There is therefore a finitely generated abelian group $M$ and a group-scheme isomorphism $E_F\simeq D_F(M)$.

source.place: Lemma 16.43, p.340, via Corollaries 12.41 (with Chapter 12 erratum) and 12.22, pp.244,239; diagonalizable classification, pp.231--234,240.

proof.text: The group $D_F(M)$ is smooth and geometrically connected by step 1. Apply [lem-sfb-diagonalizable-group-geometric-criteria]. In characteristic zero its connectedness criterion says $M$ is torsion-free. In characteristic $p>0$, geometric connectedness says every torsion element is killed by a power of $p$, while smoothness says there is no nonzero element killed by such a power; together these again say $M$ is torsion-free. The structure theorem [lem-sbc-finitely-generated-abelian-group-structure] now gives $M\simeq\mathbf Z^r$ for some $r\geq0$: every finite cyclic direct summand must be zero, since all of its elements are torsion. The product formula in [lem-sfb-diagonalizable-group-geometric-criteria] yields $E_F\simeq D_F(\mathbf Z^r)\simeq\mathbf G_m^r$. This is exactly the definition that $E$ is a $k$-torus [def-sfb-tori-multiplicative-type], including the rank-zero case.
